prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a bike stolen from the garden. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)

picture."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the loss happened overnight, I treat the timing as important evidence and look for whether the bike was present at dusk and missing by morning, since that pattern is common in garden thefts."},{"type":"fact","content":"When I see no sign of damage to the garden boundary, I do not assume the claim is weak, but I do check for other supporting detail such as neighbour sightings, CCTV or police reference."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the policyholder mentions accessories like lights, racks or a child seat, I note them separately, because
